connectorUiConfig.title: SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge Events
connectorUiConfig.descriptionMarkdown:
The SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) connector ingests CSE events (sign-ins, private access, device trust, Internet Access, malware protection, and Command Center sign-ins) from the CSE events API into the `CSEEvents_CL` table, using the Codeless Connector Framework. Events are polled every 5 minutes and usually reach Microsoft Sentinel within 10 minutes.

Events that occur while the connector is disconnected, being reconnected, or failing (for example after the API key is changed or deleted) are not fetched later. Use the SonicWall CSE backfill tool after any of these to fill the gap.

Each workspace connects to one CSE organization. To collect events from more than one CSE organization, use a separate workspace for each.

Query the data with the `CSEEvents` function installed with this solution.

properties.displayName: Parser for SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge events
properties.query:
let _OrgNames = CSEEvents_CL
    | extend _Name = tostring(RawEvent.org_name)
    | where isnotempty(_Name)
    | summarize _OrgName = take_any(_Name) by OrgId;
CSEEvents_CL
| extend _IngestedAt = ingestion_time()
| summarize arg_min(_IngestedAt, *) by EventId
| extend
    EventTime = make_datetime(1970, 1, 1) + CreatedAtMs * 1ms,
    OrgName = tostring(RawEvent.org_name),
    UserEmail = tostring(RawEvent.user_principal.user.email),
    UserName = tostring(RawEvent.user_principal.user.name),
    UserRoles = RawEvent.user_principal.user.roles,
    DeviceId = tostring(RawEvent.user_principal.device.id),
    DeviceName = tostring(RawEvent.user_principal.device.friendly_name),
    DeviceSerialNumber = tostring(RawEvent.user_principal.device.serial_number),
    DevicePlatform = tostring(RawEvent.user_principal.device.platform),
    DeviceOwnership = tostring(RawEvent.user_principal.device.ownership),
    ClientIpList = tostring(RawEvent.user_principal.client.ip_address),
    ClientUserAgent = tostring(RawEvent.user_principal.client.user_agent),
    ClientCountry = tostring(RawEvent.user_principal.client.geo_location.country),
    ClientCity = tostring(RawEvent.user_principal.client.geo_location.city),
    ServiceName = tostring(RawEvent.service.name),
    ServiceId = tostring(RawEvent.service.id),
    PolicyName = tostring(RawEvent.policy.name),
    AccessLevel = tostring(RawEvent.channel.access_level.resource),
    RequestProtocol = tostring(RawEvent.channel.request_data.protocol),
    RequestMethod = tostring(RawEvent.channel.request_data.type),
    RequestPath = tostring(RawEvent.channel.request_data.query_resources),
    SniName = tostring(RawEvent.channel.sni_data.name_requested),
    DestinationAddress = tostring(RawEvent.link.destination.ip),
    TrustLevel = tostring(RawEvent.trustscore.trust_level),
    TrustScore = toint(RawEvent.trustscore.score),
    TrustProfileName = tostring(RawEvent.trustscore.trust_profile_name),
    FailedFactors = RawEvent.trustscore.failed_factors,
    PassedFactors = RawEvent.trustscore.passed_factors,
    UrlDomain = tostring(RawEvent.url_filtering.url_details.domain),
    UrlPath = tostring(RawEvent.url_filtering.url_details.path),
    UrlFilterAction = tostring(RawEvent.url_filtering.url_filtering_result.action),
    BlockReason = tostring(RawEvent.url_filtering.url_filtering_result.block_reason),
    UrlCategory = tostring(RawEvent.url_filtering.url_filtering_result.category),
    FileHash = tostring(RawEvent.url_filtering.url_filtering_result.file_hash),
    SaasIdentity = tostring(RawEvent.url_filtering.url_filtering_result.saas_identity),
    ItpPolicyName = tostring(RawEvent.url_filtering.url_filtering_result.applied_policy.name),
    ReportedByType = tostring(RawEvent.reported_by.type),
    ReportedByHost = tostring(RawEvent.reported_by.host_name),
    AccessTierName = tostring(RawEvent.reported_by.access_tier_name)
| extend
    FailedFactors = iff(isnull(FailedFactors), dynamic([]), FailedFactors),
    PassedFactors = iff(isnull(PassedFactors), dynamic([]), PassedFactors),
    _Addresses = split(replace_regex(ClientIpList, @"\s", ""), ","),
    Message = trim_end(@"\s*\(x\d+\)\s*", Message)
| mv-apply _Address = _Addresses to typeof(string) on (
    extend _Ip = case(
        _Address matches regex @"^[0-9.]+(:\d+)?$", extract(@"^([0-9.]+)", 1, _Address),
        _Address startswith "[", extract(@"^\[([^\]]+)\]", 1, _Address),
        _Address)
    | extend _IsTunnel = coalesce(ipv4_is_in_range(_Ip, "100.64.0.0/10"), false)
    | summarize
        ClientIp = tostring(make_list_if(_Ip, isnotempty(_Ip) and not(_IsTunnel))[0]),
        TunnelIp = tostring(make_list_if(_Ip, _IsTunnel)[0])
    )
| extend FailedFactorCount = array_length(FailedFactors)
| lookup kind=leftouter _OrgNames on OrgId
| extend OrgName = iff(isempty(OrgName), _OrgName, OrgName)
| project
    TimeGenerated, EventTime, EventId, EventType, EventSubType, Action, Severity, Result, Message,
    OrgId, OrgName, CorrelationId,
    UserEmail, UserName, UserRoles,
    DeviceId, DeviceName, DeviceSerialNumber, DevicePlatform, DeviceOwnership,
    ClientIp, TunnelIp, ClientIpList, ClientUserAgent, ClientCountry, ClientCity,
    ServiceName, ServiceId, PolicyName,
    AccessLevel, RequestProtocol, RequestMethod, RequestPath, SniName, DestinationAddress,
    TrustLevel, TrustScore, TrustProfileName, FailedFactors, FailedFactorCount, PassedFactors,
    UrlDomain, UrlPath, UrlFilterAction, BlockReason, UrlCategory, FileHash, SaasIdentity, ItpPolicyName,
    ReportedByType, ReportedByHost, AccessTierName,
    CreatedAtMs, IngestedAt = _IngestedAt, RawEvent

properties.displayName: [parameters('workbook1-name')]

properties.description: SonicWallCSEConnectorHealthFailure_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.2.2

The SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) event connector reported a failed data fetch, for
example HTTP 401 after the API key was deleted or expired. While it fails, no CSE events are
ingested, and events from the failure period are not fetched later: after fixing the cause,
disconnect and connect the connector, then backfill the gap.
The rule matches both health records the poller writes: a "Data fetch status change" with
Status Failure (written once, when the status changes) and the hourly "Data fetch failure
summary" (written while failures continue). A poller that stops polling without failing
writes neither; the rule "SonicWall CSE - No events ingested" covers that case.
properties.displayName: SonicWall CSE - Event connector failing to fetch data
properties.query:
// Only records ingested since the previous run, so each record alerts once although the
// query period overlaps runs to allow for health ingestion delay.
SentinelHealth
| where ingestion_time() > ago(15m)
| where SentinelResourceType == "Data connector" and SentinelResourceKind == "ApiPolling"
| where SentinelResourceName endswith "CSEEventsPoller"
| where Status == "Failure" or OperationName == "Data fetch failure summary"
| extend Failures = ExtendedProperties.FailureSummary
| mv-expand Failure = iff(array_length(Failures) > 0, Failures, dynamic([{}]))
| extend
    StatusCode = coalesce(tostring(Failure.StatusCode), Reason),
    FailureType = tostring(Failure.HealthResultType),
    StatusMessage = coalesce(tostring(Failure.StatusMessage), Description),
    FailureStart = todatetime(ExtendedProperties.StartTime),
    FailureEnd = todatetime(ExtendedProperties.EndTime)
| project TimeGenerated, SentinelResourceName, OperationName, Status, StatusCode, FailureType,
    StatusMessage, FailureStart, FailureEnd, SentinelResourceId

properties.description: SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge Analytics Rule 1

properties.displayName: SonicWall CSE - Event connector failing to fetch data

properties.description: SonicWallCSEDeviceTrustAlwaysDeny_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.2.2

A device's SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) trust level changed to AlwaysDeny, so the device
is denied access to protected resources. Causes include failed trust factors (for example
disk encryption or firewall turned off), no trust profile matching the device ("Default"),
or an administrator ban. Alerts once per change: the trust state repeats on every Service
Tunnel event, so only TrustScoring events are evaluated, and an evaluation that stays at
AlwaysDeny does not alert again.
Evaluates events by when they reached Sentinel, so events that arrive late (connector
delay or a backfill) are evaluated once, when they arrive. The query period is 2 days to
include backfilled events, which keep their own time for up to 48 hours.
properties.displayName: SonicWall CSE - Device trust level dropped to AlwaysDeny
properties.query:
let RunWindow = 1h;
CSEEvents
| where EventType == "TrustScoring" and isnotempty(DeviceSerialNumber)
| order by DeviceSerialNumber asc, EventTime asc
| extend PreviousLevel = iff(prev(DeviceSerialNumber) == DeviceSerialNumber, prev(TrustLevel), "")
| where TrustLevel == "AlwaysDeny" and PreviousLevel != "AlwaysDeny"
| where IngestedAt > ago(RunWindow)
| project TimeGenerated, EventTime, Action, DeviceSerialNumber, DeviceName, DevicePlatform, UserEmail,
    PreviousLevel, TrustLevel, TrustScore, TrustProfileName, FailedFactors, EventId
| extend
    AccountName = tostring(split(UserEmail, "@")[0]),
    UPNSuffix = tostring(split(UserEmail, "@")[1]),
    HostName = coalesce(DeviceName, DeviceSerialNumber),
    FailedFactorList = strcat_array(FailedFactors, ", ")

alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: SonicWall CSE: device {{HostName}} trust level AlwaysDeny
alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: Trust level changed from {{PreviousLevel}} to AlwaysDeny. Failed factors: {{FailedFactorList}}.

properties.description: SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge Analytics Rule 2

properties.displayName: SonicWall CSE - Device trust level dropped to AlwaysDeny

properties.description: SonicWallCSEFailedAdminLogin_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.2.2

A sign-in to the SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) Command Center failed (AdminLogin Deny).
CSE logs failed admin logins at INFO severity, so alerting on severity misses them. Admin
sign-in normally goes through MySonicWall single sign-on; a failed sign-in with a local
account, such as the built-in provisioning account, deserves review.
Evaluates events by when they reached Sentinel, so events that arrive late (connector
delay or a backfill) are evaluated once, when they arrive. The query period is 2 days to
include backfilled events, which keep their own time for up to 48 hours.
properties.displayName: SonicWall CSE - Failed Command Center admin login
properties.query:
CSEEvents
| where IngestedAt > ago(1h)
| where EventType == "AdminLogin" and Action == "Deny"
| summarize
    FailedLogins = count(),
    FirstFailure = min(EventTime),
    LastFailure = max(EventTime),
    SubTypes = make_set(EventSubType),
    ClientIps = make_set_if(ClientIp, isnotempty(ClientIp), 10),
    ClientIp = take_anyif(ClientIp, isnotempty(ClientIp)),
    UserAgent = take_any(ClientUserAgent)
    by UserEmail, UserName
| extend
    AccountName = tostring(split(UserEmail, "@")[0]),
    UPNSuffix = tostring(split(UserEmail, "@")[1])

alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: SonicWall CSE: {{FailedLogins}} failed admin login(s) for {{UserEmail}}
alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: Failed Command Center sign-in for {{UserEmail}} between {{FirstFailure}} and {{LastFailure}}.

properties.description: SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge Analytics Rule 3

properties.displayName: SonicWall CSE - Failed Command Center admin login

properties.description: SonicWallCSEMalwareBlocked_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.2.2

SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) Malware Download Protection blocked a file download as
malicious (Malware Denied). The user's device attempted to download a malicious file; check
how the user reached the source and whether other copies were obtained another way.
Logged at INFO severity. Malware events can reach the API up to about 10 minutes after they
occur.
Evaluates events by when they reached Sentinel, so events that arrive late (connector
delay or a backfill) are evaluated once, when they arrive. The query period is 2 days to
include backfilled events, which keep their own time for up to 48 hours.
properties.displayName: SonicWall CSE - Malware download blocked
properties.query:
CSEEvents
| where EventType == "Malware" and Action == "Denied"
| where IngestedAt > ago(1h)
| project TimeGenerated, EventTime, UserEmail, DeviceSerialNumber, DeviceName, ClientIp, UrlDomain, UrlPath,
    BlockReason, FileHash, ItpPolicyName, Message, EventId
| extend
    AccountName = tostring(split(UserEmail, "@")[0]),
    UPNSuffix = tostring(split(UserEmail, "@")[1]),
    HostName = coalesce(DeviceName, DeviceSerialNumber),
    Url = strcat("https://", UrlDomain, UrlPath)

alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: SonicWall CSE: malware download blocked from {{UrlDomain}}

properties.description: SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge Analytics Rule 4

properties.displayName: SonicWall CSE - Malware download blocked

properties.description: SonicWallCSENoEventsIngested_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.2.2

No SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) events have been ingested for longer than the
threshold. It complements the health rule: it does not depend on health monitoring being
enabled, and it also fires when the connector is disconnected or ingestion stops for a reason
the connector does not report (for example the workspace daily cap).
Possible causes: the connector stopped polling or was disconnected, the API key is invalid,
the workspace daily cap was reached, or CSE produced no events. Check the connector, then
compare with the CSE events API before assuming data was lost.
Set QuietThreshold to the longest normal quiet period for the organization; a short threshold
also fires during quiet periods, such as nights or weekends with no CSE activity. Outages
shorter than the threshold are reported by the connector health rule.
properties.displayName: SonicWall CSE - No events ingested

alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: SonicWall CSE: no events ingested since {{LastIngested}}
alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: No CSE events ingested for more than the threshold. Last ingestion: {{LastIngested}}.

properties.description: SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge Analytics Rule 5

properties.displayName: SonicWall CSE - No events ingested

properties.description: SonicWallCSERepeatedAccessDenials_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.2.2

One user was denied by SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) repeatedly within an hour: blocked
connections or requests (Access Unauthorized) and refused sign-ins (Identity Deny), for
example a revoked certificate, a trust score that is too low, or roles with no access to the
service. Repeated denials can indicate a compromised or non-compliant device, an account
trying resources it is not entitled to, or a misconfigured policy.
Matches on type and action, not severity. Each event counts once. Denials are counted per hour of event time.
Evaluates events by when they reached Sentinel, so events that arrive late (connector
delay or a backfill) are evaluated once, when they arrive. The query period is 2 days to
include backfilled events, which keep their own time for up to 48 hours.
properties.displayName: SonicWall CSE - Repeated access denials for one user
properties.query:
let DenialThreshold = 5;
CSEEvents
| where IngestedAt > ago(1h)
| where (EventType == "Access" and Action == "Unauthorized")
    or (EventType == "Identity" and Action == "Deny")
| where isnotempty(UserEmail)
| summarize
    Denials = count(),
    FirstDenial = min(EventTime),
    LastDenial = max(EventTime),
    Reasons = make_set(Message, 10),
    Services = make_set_if(ServiceName, isnotempty(ServiceName), 10),
    Devices = make_set_if(DeviceName, isnotempty(DeviceName), 5),
    DeviceSerialNumber = take_anyif(DeviceSerialNumber, isnotempty(DeviceSerialNumber)),
    ClientIp = take_anyif(ClientIp, isnotempty(ClientIp))
    by UserEmail, Hour = bin(EventTime, 1h)
| where Denials >= DenialThreshold
| extend
    AccountName = tostring(split(UserEmail, "@")[0]),
    UPNSuffix = tostring(split(UserEmail, "@")[1]),
    HostName = coalesce(tostring(Devices[0]), DeviceSerialNumber)

properties.description: SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge Analytics Rule 6

properties.displayName: SonicWall CSE - Repeated access denials for one user

properties.description: SonicWallCSESignInNewCountry_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.2.2

A user signed in to, or was refused by, SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) from a country not
seen for that user in the previous 14 days. This can indicate stolen credentials or a stolen
device, and also normal travel. Users with no earlier sign-ins in the period are skipped, so
new users do not alert; the "New users" hunting query lists them.
Evaluates events by when they reached Sentinel, so events that arrive late (connector
delay or a backfill) are evaluated once, when they arrive. Country is from the CSE sign-in
event (Identity events); the query period of 14 days is the history compared against.
properties.displayName: SonicWall CSE - Sign-in from a new country for a user
properties.query:
let RunWindow = 1h;
let SignIns = CSEEvents
    | where EventType == "Identity" and Action in ("Grant", "Deny")
    | where isnotempty(UserEmail) and isnotempty(ClientCountry);
let Known = SignIns
    | where IngestedAt <= ago(RunWindow)
    | summarize KnownCountries = make_set(ClientCountry, 50) by UserEmail;
SignIns
| where IngestedAt > ago(RunWindow)
| join kind=inner Known on UserEmail
| where not(set_has_element(KnownCountries, ClientCountry))
| summarize
    SignIns = count(),
    Granted = countif(Action == "Grant"),
    FirstSeen = min(EventTime),
    LastSeen = max(EventTime),
    Cities = make_set_if(ClientCity, isnotempty(ClientCity), 5),
    ClientIp = take_anyif(ClientIp, isnotempty(ClientIp)),
    Devices = make_set_if(DeviceName, isnotempty(DeviceName), 5),
    KnownCountries = take_any(KnownCountries)
    by UserEmail, ClientCountry
| extend
    AccountName = tostring(split(UserEmail, "@")[0]),
    UPNSuffix = tostring(split(UserEmail, "@")[1])

alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: SonicWall CSE: {{UserEmail}} signed in from a new country, {{ClientCountry}}
alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: First sign-in from {{ClientCountry}} for {{UserEmail}} in 14 days, at {{FirstSeen}}.

properties.description: SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge Analytics Rule 7

properties.displayName: SonicWall CSE - Sign-in from a new country for a user

properties.displayName: SonicWall CSE - New users
properties.query:
let Lookback = 14d;
let Recent = 1d;
CSEEvents
| where EventTime > ago(Lookback) and isnotempty(UserEmail)
| summarize
    FirstSeen = min(EventTime),
    LastSeen = max(EventTime),
    Events = count(),
    Devices = make_set_if(DeviceName, isnotempty(DeviceName), 10),
    Countries = make_set_if(ClientCountry, isnotempty(ClientCountry), 10),
    ClientIp = take_anyif(ClientIp, isnotempty(ClientIp))
    by UserEmail

| extend
    AccountName = tostring(split(UserEmail, "@")[0]),
    UPNSuffix = tostring(split(UserEmail, "@")[1])

properties.descriptionHtml:
Note: Please refer to the following before installing the solution:

• Review the solution Release Notes

• There may be known issues pertaining to this Solution, please refer to them before installing.

The SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) solution ingests CSE events into Microsoft Sentinel through the CSE events API, and includes a parser, a workbook, analytic rules, and hunting queries for CSE sign-ins, private access, device trust, and Internet Access.

Underlying Microsoft Technologies used:

This solution takes a dependency on the following technologies, and some of these dependencies either may be in Preview state or might result in additional ingestion or operational costs:

  1. Codeless Connector Framework

  2. Azure Monitor Logs Ingestion API

Data Connectors: 1, Parsers: 1, Workbooks: 1, Analytic Rules: 7, Hunting Queries: 6
